executive_summary.headline: World models and long video are the creator story
executive_summary.body: Genie 4 turns a prompt into a world you can steer with sound, and @rpn frames it as robot practice. Instagram began testing Features, 90-minute horizontal video where Reels act as trailers, and creators are already telling followers to batch their clips.

executive_summary.headline: Computer use gets cheap enough for the back office
executive_summary.body: GPT-6.1 Terra is priced 50% below its predecessor and creators show it typing invoices into accounting software. Gemini now creates and edits files inside the chat for personal Google accounts, and an AI agent phoned 848 local businesses in one reporter's account.

executive_summary.headline: Scientists get new ways in: free credits, grants and robot labs
executive_summary.body: Linköping used AI to find 33 hidden MXenes and make 11 new ones, Anthropic gave 20 science groups free Claude credits, and Nottingham built a two-robot lab for heat-resistant coatings. Meta put $2 million and model access behind five universities.

top_picks.title: Roberto Nickson explains why Genie 4 matters for robots, not just games
top_picks.summary: Genie 4 generates interactive worlds with sound and dialogue that react in real time, and @rpn argues the real prize is robot training: machines can practice millions of times in generated worlds before touching the real one. Google DeepMind's post says Genie 4 steers worlds in real time, adds native audio and uses Gemini 3.8 Flash to guide simulations, in a research preview for trusted testers.
top_picks.author: @rpn (Roberto Nickson)
top_picks.enterprise_translation: Practice-in-simulation is the idea to borrow. Before any physical trial, let an agent or a new hire rehearse the task in a generated scene. Prompt a world model or any scenario generator with one process you run (a loading dock, a test rig, a customer visit) and watch what the rehearsal gets wrong.
top_picks.why_it_matters: @rpn is on the TikTok and Instagram watch list; the claim about robot practice is his framing, the product facts are from DeepMind's post.

top_picks.title: Instagram tests Features: 90-minute horizontal video, with Reels as the trailer
top_picks.summary: Instagram began testing Features on October 26: horizontal videos up to 90 minutes for podcasts, interviews and full shows, shown in the main feed and Explore. Creators can cut Reels from a Feature that link back to the full video, and the test starts with select US creators and some in Brazil.
top_picks.author: @tech_takeaways
top_picks.enterprise_translation: Short clip as trailer, long video as the product. Record one long internal explainer or demo, cut the best 60 seconds as a teaser and track how many viewers click through to the full version.
top_picks.why_it_matters: This is a platform format change rather than an AI model release; creators are already using AI clip tools to feed it.

top_picks.title: GPT-6.1 Terra can see your screen and type invoices into accounting software
top_picks.summary: @manavpod's Reel says GPT-6.1 Terra uses desktop apps, like typing invoices into accounting software, and scored 15 points higher than GPT-5.6 Terra on Agents' Last Exam at about a third of the cost. OpenAI's launch page lists $1 per million input tokens, 50% below GPT-5.6 Terra, and 50.3% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 at maximum effort.
top_picks.author: @manavpod
top_picks.enterprise_translation: Computer use is now cheap enough for the dull jobs. Pick one repetitive screen task, like re-keying invoices or copying data between two portals, and hand it to Terra for an afternoon to see how many rows it clears.
top_picks.category: New capability / small business back office

top_picks.title: Linköping team uses AI to find 33 hidden MXenes and make 11 new ones in seconds
top_picks.summary: Researchers at Linköping University used AI searches of older materials databases to identify 33 existing MXenes, then created 11 new ones with a synthesis method that needs no external heating and takes seconds. The work was published in Science and the university says the method uses far fewer hazardous chemicals and less water.
top_picks.author: Linköping University (Johanna Rosen et al.)
top_picks.enterprise_translation: Mine your own old data before running new experiments. Point a model at ten years of archived test results and ask which compositions nobody followed up on, then pick two for a quick bench test.
top_picks.why_it_matters: Science bonus applied: AI-guided materials discovery published in a peer-reviewed journal.

top_picks.title: Anthropic gives 20 science foundations and institutions free Claude credits
top_picks.summary: Anthropic is expanding its AI for Science program to 20 scientific foundations, institutions and research groups, providing free Claude credits to support their work. The program began in May 2025 and the post names projects including the gnomAD database of DNA data from over 800,000 people.
top_picks.author: Anthropic
top_picks.enterprise_translation: Credits plus a named partner is how other labs get scientists to try AI. Offer a small R&D group a funded sandbox and one shared problem from their backlog, then compare what they ship in a month.
top_picks.why_it_matters: Science bonus applied: a model for how a funder gets research groups using AI.

top_picks.title: Gemini now creates, previews and edits documents, PDFs, sheets and slides inside the chat
top_picks.summary: Google says Gemini can generate, preview and edit files directly in chat, with PDF preview and editing on web and mobile and other formats on web. It is available to Workspace customers, Workspace Individual subscribers and personal Google account users.
top_picks.author: Google Workspace team
top_picks.enterprise_translation: The chat window becomes the document editor. Ask Gemini to turn a messy meeting note into a formatted one-pager, then edit it by chatting instead of copying text into another app.

sections.title: LinkedIn
sections.description: No significant AI content this week on LinkedIn. LinkedIn post pages for October 26 to November 1 were not reachable through our fetch tools (the search index and the George's Blog LinkedIn mirror stopped at October 24), so this section is empty rather than filled with older posts.

sections.title: TikTok and short-form video
sections.description: TikTok pages block automated reads, so engagement numbers were not available. These two items are the closest verifiable how-to content for formats spreading on TikTok.

items.title: A builder publishes the recipe behind a viral Tiny Desk AI parody clip with Wan 3.0 and Seedance 2.5
items.summary: The author ran 25 test renders on October 26 and 27 to build a 19-second, five-shot vertical clip: 571 frames at 30 fps, with Wan 3.0 for 480p and 720p and Seedance 2.5 for 1080p. The Tiny Desk format is the AI video style spreading on TikTok and Reels this month.
items.author: codeugar
items.enterprise_translation: A format is a template you can steal. Pick a recognizable setup, swap in your own subject, and render five short shots for an internal product teaser using the same open video models.
items.why_it_matters: TikTok pages block automated reads, so this is the closest verifiable how-to for the format; it is a Hugging Face post, not a TikTok post.

items.title: Taro Creates walks through automating TikTok Shop videos with Claude at about $1 each
items.summary: The creator says one TikTok Shop account made $200,000 in revenue and sold nearly 12,000 units in 30 days, and that his batch of 15 short product videos, typically 5 to 10 seconds, costs about $1 per video with Claude and Niche credits. These are the creator's own figures in a 21-minute YouTube walkthrough.
items.author: Taro Creates
items.enterprise_translation: Cheap batches turn video into an experiment you can repeat. Generate fifteen short product clips for one SKU, post them over a week and keep the hooks that held viewers.

sections.title: Instagram
sections.description: Reels and posts from AI explainers and creators, with likes where the page showed them.

items.title: @msbintel's Claude Duet Reel offers a setup guide for anyone who comments DUET
items.summary: @msbintel says Duet starts with the memory, skills and connected apps you already set up in Claude, then sends a morning brief and works in the cloud. The Reel drew 4,118 likes and dozens of one-word DUET comments within eight hours.
items.author: @msbintel
items.enterprise_translation: One-word comment as the sign-up form. Run a post that offers a checklist for a single keyword and count how many people raise a hand, whether for customers or for an internal AI-tools clinic.
items.recurrence_note: Claude Duet was a Top Pick last week; this week the story is creators turning it into lead-generation Reels.

items.title: @mr.eflow tests Genie 4 and reports sharp visuals, with the Mustang turning into a taxi
items.summary: @mr.eflow says Genie 4 looks realistic and lets you prompt anything into the world, while the monkey, car and biplane ignored steering and a Mustang changed direction when he turned around. Commenters proposed a lost-keys test: leave keys on a table, explore for a minute and come back.
items.author: @mr.eflow
items.enterprise_translation: A comeback test is a cheap benchmark for any new model. Put an object in a scene, look away and look back, then borrow the same trick on the next tool you evaluate.

items.title: @ai.jitendra's plan: record one long video, post the best 60 seconds as Reels, link them on day one
items.summary: The Reel explains that up to 8 short clips can point back to one long Features video, that the test is small and US-based after a trial in Brazil, and that Instagram has announced no ad-revenue share per Variety. The creator's advice is to prepare one long video and its clips ahead of access.
items.author: @ai.jitendra
items.enterprise_translation: Batch the clips before the feature reaches you. Write the long script, then mark eight moments that work alone and you have a month of posts from one recording session.

items.title: Google's own Genie 4 Reel: create, hear and steer interactive simulations in real time
items.summary: Google says Genie 4 is rolling out as a research preview to trusted testers, with Google AI Ultra subscribers getting it soon in Project Genie and early access partners in the Gemini API and Google AI Studio. Commenters asked what testers try first: building their own worlds or testing how agents behave inside them.
items.author: @newsfromgoogle
items.enterprise_translation: Ask what you would drop an agent into first. Write down three environments you would like an assistant to rehearse in (a warehouse, a lab bench, a support queue), then rank them by how much practice would help.

sections.title: Facebook
sections.description: Meta's newsroom, which publishes to Facebook. Facebook video pages did not expose reliable dates this week.

items.title: Meta backs five universities with $2 million and its latest models for medical and scientific work
items.summary: Meta is giving $2 million in grants and model access to Caltech, Ohio State College of Medicine, Louisiana State University, Indiana University and UTHealth Houston. Projects include LSU computer vision for infant tracheostomy tubes, Indiana multimodal AI for dementia care and Ohio State heart-failure prediction from CT scans.
items.author: Meta
items.enterprise_translation: Small grants plus real models get researchers experimenting fast. Fund two or three tightly scoped pilots with a university lab or your own scientists, each aimed at one measurable outcome.
items.why_it_matters: Science bonus applied: researcher adoption through grants and model access.

sections.title: AI for Science
sections.description: Materials, coatings and lab-automation stories from universities and companies this week. Linköping's MXenes work and Anthropic's science program are in Top Picks.

items.title: Nottingham builds a two-robot self-driving lab for heat-resistant thermal barrier coatings
items.summary: The University of Nottingham's coating group built a lab with two robotic arms and a liquid-dispensing tool that prepares a precursor solution, runs furnace processing, controls cooling and retrieves the sample. AI active learning helped identify and prepare several candidate pyrochlore materials, in a paper in Engineering Applications of Artificial Intelligence.
items.author: Centre of Excellence in Coating and Surface Engineering
items.enterprise_translation: Coatings and surface materials are a natural fit for a robot that never gets bored. Map one formulation-and-cure workflow your lab repeats weekly and ask which steps an arm and a scheduler could take over.
items.category: AI for science / materials and coatings
items.why_it_matters: Science bonus applied: materials and coatings R&D with lab automation.

items.title: Radical AI and Wiley link 195,359 papers to a materials discovery platform
items.summary: Radical's workflows incorporate 195,359 Wiley papers, and the company reports 1,000+ novel material candidates, including more than 300 in a first hypersonic-material campaign. Radical says it beat an industry-leading hypersonic material within 16 weeks and generated 70 million experimental data points.
items.author: Radical AI and Wiley
items.enterprise_translation: Publisher archives become training fuel. Give a model your own internal reports and a licensed journal set, and ask it for ten candidate materials ranked against one performance target.
items.why_it_matters: Science bonus applied. Figures are the company's own claims.

items.title: Cambridge joins the founding lab network of CuspAI's AI Materials Foundry
items.summary: The University of Cambridge's materials department joined the founding lab network of CuspAI's AI Materials Foundry, led there by Associate Professor Shijing Sun, whose group works on autonomous materials discovery. The targets are materials for semiconductors, clean energy and advanced manufacturing.
items.author: Department of Materials Science & Metallurgy
items.enterprise_translation: A network of labs sharing one AI platform scales faster than one lab alone. Pair your scientists with an outside group on a shared materials problem and compare results after a quarter.

sections.title: Creator, Indie and Small-Business Signals
sections.description: Voice agents, no-code builders and API credits for solo builders.

items.title: An AI agent phoned 848 local businesses and about one in three stayed on the line
items.summary: San Francisco Standard reports that Voygr's AI agent made 848 phone calls to local businesses, about one in three respondents stayed on the phone after learning it was an AI, and 1 in 25 businesses already had an AI agent answering. A Mastercard executive notes about 96% of small businesses bring in under $1 million a year.
items.author: Jessica Blough
items.enterprise_translation: Voice agents now do the boring phone round. List the calls your team makes just to confirm hours, stock or prices and try an agent on a batch of ten.

items.title: Emergent says 18 million apps are built on its platform and 200,000 are live
items.summary: In an Economic Times interview posted on Emergent's site, CEO Mukund Jha says small businesses that ran on spreadsheets, email and WhatsApp now build their own software. The company reports its valuation rose from $300 million to $1.5 billion between January and July, with over 40 million monthly visitors to live apps.
items.author: Emergent (Mukund Jha interview)
items.enterprise_translation: Nontechnical owners are the new software builders. Pick one spreadsheet that runs a team process and prompt a no-code builder to turn it into a small app in one sitting.

items.title: ChatGPT Pro and Business subscribers can claim up to $500 a month in API credits
items.summary: Digg relays OpenAI's October 28 offer: eligible ChatGPT Pro and Business subscribers can claim up to $500 per month in API credits to build apps and agents, usable on GPT Live, Image 2.5 and the Decisions API. A source post lists Pro credits of $100, $200 or $500 monthly and Business credits of $20 per Standard seat or $100 per Premium seat.
items.author: OpenAI via Digg
items.enterprise_translation: Subscriptions that include build credit make weekend projects free. Claim the credit and spend it on one tiny agent you have wanted for months.

emerging_signals.pattern: Short clips are becoming trailers for long video
emerging_signals.evidence: Instagram's Features test pairs 90-minute videos with Reels that link back, and creator explainers from @tech_takeaways and @ai.jitendra tell people to prepare clips ahead of access. Hugging Face's Tiny Desk recipe shows the same five-shot, short-first logic.
emerging_signals.what_to_watch: Whether Instagram widens access beyond select US and Brazil creators.

emerging_signals.evidence: @msbintel's Duet Reel reached 4,118 likes with dozens of one-word DUET comments, and @worldof.aix used the same format for Opus and Terra posts.
emerging_signals.what_to_watch: Which launches stop generating keyword replies as the format saturates.

emerging_signals.pattern: World models are pitched as practice grounds
emerging_signals.evidence: @rpn frames Genie 4 as robot training, Google's Reel says robots and agents could learn before helping out in real life, and commenters propose persistence tests.
emerging_signals.what_to_watch: The first Genie 4 tests by independent builders in Project Genie and the Gemini API.

emerging_signals.pattern: Computer use gets a price cut that fits the back office
emerging_signals.evidence: GPT-6.1 Terra is listed at $1 per million input tokens, 50% below its predecessor, and creators describe it typing invoices into accounting software.
emerging_signals.what_to_watch: First small-business write-ups with time saved per task.

emerging_signals.pattern: Self-driving labs reach coatings and materials foundries
emerging_signals.evidence: Nottingham's two-robot coatings lab, Cambridge joining CuspAI's foundry network and Radical AI's literature-driven pipeline were all announced within three days.
emerging_signals.what_to_watch: Whether any group publishes bench-validated results for a building or industrial material.

sources_to_add: A signed-in cloud browser session for TikTok and LinkedIn so view counts and post pages can be read
Instagram hashtag pages such as #genie4 and #aitools for daily sampling
Company newsrooms (Meta, Google, Anthropic) as primary anchors for platform items
topics_to_add: Building-science and materials-lab posts on LinkedIn and Instagram
Small-business owners posting before-and-after numbers from AI agents
topics_to_drop: Launch-day Reels with fewer than 10 likes unless they add a hands-on workflow
suggested_refinements.notes: Access limits this week: LinkedIn post pages for the window were not reachable, TikTok blocks automated reads (no videos or counts), and Facebook video pages gave no reliable dates. Instagram dates come from the page crawl date minus the age shown, and likes were read from the page where shown (many Reels hide counts). Several items are press or company pages rather than social posts: Linköping, Anthropic, Google Workspace, Meta Newsroom, Nottingham, Wiley, Cambridge, San Francisco Standard, Emergent and Digg. GPT-6.1 Terra, YouTube and Forbes pages returned 403 or 429 to a plain HTTP request but rendered the matching content through our fetch tool. The requested model claude_sonnet_5_0 was unavailable and claude_sonnet_5_5 was substituted.
